answer: Anchor each agent identity to scarce hardware: a new agent registers through a verified peer — a "jetty" gateway with bounded capacity and a real operator — issuing one credential per identity after a short proof-of-work. Those credentials form a public haven of accountable identities, so anyone can verify a counterparty traces back to a real gateway. When a gale of fake registrations arrives, the attacker cannot spawn ten thousand sybils: each fake needs its own credential from a gateway with capped, logged throughput, and flooding the network means buying machines — costly, leaving a trail.
